title: Sandridge Road / Lake Asbury / First Coast Expressway land & development activity
description: District 5's Lake Asbury area is undergoing rapid change: the county-funded Sandridge Road (CR 739B) widening ($31.6M, per the county's own project page), a 2005 Lake Asbury Master Plan, a 2021 moratorium on new rezoning within the master-plan area, growth pressure tied to the First Coast Expressway, and a 2025 inter-neighborhood "connectivity" rezoning-adjacent plan that was withdrawn after public opposition. The lead is whether specific land sales, rezonings, or comprehensive-plan amendments in this corridor show a pattern connecting county infrastructure spending, private landowners/developers, and BCC/District 5 decisions.
origin: User-provided investigative lead (mission brief), refined against initial search research 2026-09-11.
entitiesInvolved: Clay County Public Works / Bonded Transportation Program
whyItMatters: Road-widening and rezoning decisions directly affect adjacent land values; if any BCC vote or land-use approval in this corridor coincided with a documented financial or personal relationship, that intersection would be a Voting-Conflict/Ethics lead, not by itself an allegation.
evidenceAvailable: Official county project page for the Sandridge Road widening (source: county Bonded Transportation Program). News coverage of the 2025 connectivity-plan withdrawal and general Lake Asbury growth pressure (secondary).
evidenceMissing: No parcel-level ownership chain (property appraiser → seller → buyer → LLC) has been built. No specific rezoning/comprehensive-plan-amendment case tied to this corridor has been pulled from BCC agendas/minutes. No confirmation of Burke's specific votes on any Lake Asbury/Sandridge-corridor item.
recordsNeeded: Clay County Property Appraiser parcel records for land adjacent to the Sandridge Road corridor
BCC agenda/minutes for all Lake Asbury Master Plan amendments and rezonings, 2019-present
The withdrawn 2025 "connectivity" plan application and who submitted it
Sunbiz records for any LLC that acquired land in this corridor during the widening project

title: Gustafson family / company connections to Clay County land and development matters
description: RESOLVED (core facts) 2026-09-11 via primary source: on June 24, 2025 the BCC denied (4-1) Sheryl Edlyn Gustafson's request (COMP 25-0010 / ZON 25-0007) to change 13.86 acres at 2005 S CR 16-A, Green Cove Springs (The Springs planning district, District 5) from Agriculture to Rural Residential/AR, despite staff, the Planning Commission (6-0), and the Springs Citizens Advisory Committee (6-0) all recommending approval. Vice-Chairman Kristen Burke personally made the motion to deny; Commissioner John Sgromolo seconded; Commissioner Jim Renninger was the lone dissenting vote (opposed to the denial). The property is Gustafson's own homesteaded residence since 2013, acquired via nominal-consideration family/trust transfers in 2012, not a recent outside-developer acquisition. NOTE: this parcel (CR 16-A / The Springs) is geographically distinct from the Sandridge Road / Lake Asbury corridor in LEAD-sandridge — do not conflate the two areas. Whether there is any broader Gustafson family/company footprint in Clay County beyond this one case remains open.
origin: User-provided investigative lead (mission brief). Core facts verified against official BCC minutes and Property Appraiser records 2026-09-11.
whyItMatters: This is now the investigation's best-documented single BCC action involving Burke: a motion she personally made, against staff/CAC/Planning-Commission recommendations, in her own district. Recorded neutrally — voting/moving against a staff recommendation is a normal, lawful exercise of a commissioner's discretion, not evidence of impropriety by itself. Whether there is a broader Gustafson pattern (beyond this one homesteaded family parcel) remains the open question.
evidenceAvailable: Official, e-signed BCC minutes (PrimeGov meetingTemplateId 8164) with full case detail, motion/second/vote, and a video timestamp (1:56:56-2:20:20). Official Property Appraiser parcel record (16-06-26-015574-001-02) with ownership and sale history back to 2012. The original CitizenPortal.ai lead is now confirmed partially accurate (topline facts) and partially wrong (commissioner names) — see EV-004/EV-010/EV-011/EV-012.
evidenceMissing: No confirmation of any OTHER Gustafson-connected parcel, business, or BCC matter beyond this one case. G Bar Ranch LLC / G Bar Ranch South LLC (the 2012 grantor, likely a Gustafson-family ranching entity) has not been independently confirmed via Sunbiz. No re-application (PUD or reduced-density) has been filed or found yet, per Chairman Condon's suggestion at the hearing.
recordsNeeded: Sunbiz detail for G Bar Ranch LLC / G Bar Ranch South LLC to confirm the Gustafson-family ranching-entity connection
A general Clay County land-record and BCC-agenda name search for 'Gustafson' beyond this one case, to establish or rule out a broader footprint
Any follow-up PUD or reduced-density re-application for this parcel

title: Burke chiropractic/business interests — including a reported newer clinic possibly involving a family member
description: Kristen Burke is a chiropractor and, per her practice's own site, has co-owned Fleming Island Family Chiropractic with her husband Harold Burke since 2000 — that fact is well-established and not itself in question. Separately, there is an UNVERIFIED lead that a different, more recently opened chiropractic clinic may involve Burke's brother and/or other family members. No such clinic has been identified by name yet, and no ownership/management link to Burke has been found.
origin: User-provided investigative lead (mission brief). Existing practice confirmed 2026-09-11; the 'newer clinic / brother' claim not yet substantiated.
whyItMatters: If a Burke-family-connected business later sought or received a county permit, zoning approval, or other BCC action, that would be a Voting-Conflict/Ethics lead. Nothing found so far establishes that any such action has occurred.
evidenceAvailable: Self-published bio on Fleming Island Family Chiropractic's own website confirming Kristen + Harold Burke opened that practice in 2000. Fleming Island Family Chiropractic, Inc. confirmed active in Sunbiz (P00000100632) 2026-09-11, though officer detail wasn't pulled (automation friction). The practice donated $1,000 + $364.31 in-kind to Burke's own 2020 campaign (EV-014). Two campaign donors share the Burke surname — Kenneth Burke ($100) and Laurie Burke ($200) — unverified as relatives (EV-017). A same-named 'Burke Chiropractic LLC' was found and DISPROVEN as connected (St. Petersburg, FL, owners James L. and Sarah E. Burke — EV-016).

Fleming Island Family Chiropractic, Inc.'s Sunbiz officer/registered-agent detail has not been pulled. No confirmation of whether Kenneth Burke or Laurie Burke (2020 campaign donors) are related to Kristen Burke.

title: Stormwater assessment decision-making and Burke's role as Board Chair
description: Clay County adopted a new stormwater assessment fee (based on impervious surface area, roughly $51-$161/year for a single-family home) alongside hardship and disabled-veteran exemptions. News coverage describes Board Chair Kristen Burke chairing a contentious public hearing, described as frustrated with attendees and threatening to eject people for clapping or speaking out of turn. ClayMoneyTrail's existing money-trail dataset already carries the official stormwater revenue/cost estimates (sourceId: stormwater-impact) — this lead is about the decision-making process and Burke's specific role, not the dollar figures, which are handled in the main money-trail dataset.
origin: User-provided investigative lead (mission brief). Confirmed as a real, documented controversy 2026-09-11.
whyItMatters: Establishes the factual public record of how the assessment was adopted and how the Board Chair conducted the process, distinct from any claim about the fee's legality or fairness.
evidenceAvailable: Multiple secondary news accounts (Action News Jax, WOKV) of hearings, exemption votes, and Burke's conduct as chair. Official county business-impact estimate already in ClayMoneyTrail's money dataset.
evidenceMissing: No official meeting minutes/video timestamp has been pulled to independently confirm the specific conduct described by news outlets. No full vote history (who voted for/against the assessment and each exemption) has been compiled. No confirmation of where stormwater revenue is actually being spent (vs. budgeted) yet exists.
recordsNeeded: Official BCC meeting video/minutes for the stormwater assessment adoption vote and the hardship/veteran exemption vote, with timestamps
Full commissioner-by-commissioner vote record for each stormwater-related agenda item
Actual (not budgeted) stormwater collections and expenditures once available

title: Commissioner compensation increase proposal
description: Clay County commissioner salary has been fixed at $37,000/year since 2008 per the Home Rule Charter (already documented in ClayMoneyTrail's main dataset, sourceId: county-charter). The Charter Review Commission — a separate advisory body from the BCC itself — has reportedly discussed raising it, with different secondary sources citing figures from roughly $60,000 up to 'triple' the current salary, and reporting Charter Review Chair Courtney Connor opposed. Whether Burke has personally advocated for or against any specific figure has not been established.
origin: User-provided investigative lead (mission brief). Proposal's existence confirmed 2026-09-11; Burke's position not yet established.
whyItMatters: The mission brief explicitly warns not to attribute this proposal to Burke unless records establish that — this lead exists specifically to check that attribution, not assume it.
evidenceAvailable: Secondary news coverage (Clay Views, Action News Jax) describing the Charter Review Commission's discussion and a range of proposed figures.
evidenceMissing: No primary Charter Review Commission agenda/minutes has been pulled. No statement or vote by Burke specifically on this proposal has been found. The exact proposed figure is inconsistent across secondary sources and needs reconciling against the primary record.
recordsNeeded: Official Charter Review Commission agenda/minutes for the compensation discussion, with the exact proposed figure and calculation method
Confirmation of whether this requires a ballot measure and its current status
Any recorded statement or vote by Burke specifically on this proposal
